summary: Relate piston-ring gap closure and a specified tangential closing force to rectangular section properties, mean cylinder-wall pressure, and equivalent normal contact force.

problemStatement:
An engineering team is reviewing a representative single-piece cast-iron compression piston ring for an automotive internal-combustion engine. The ring is manufactured with a free end gap m. During installation it is compressed into a nominally circular cylinder bore, reducing the gap to s and producing outward contact with the cylinder wall.

For this simplified MEEN 305 model, the tangential closing force Ft is a specified piston-ring parameter. Use it to determine the mean/equivalent cylinder-wall pressure; do not derive it from m − s with a straight-beam equation. The context photograph is representative and is not claimed to show the assigned numerical ring.
engineeringGoal: Determine the free-to-installed gap closure, rectangular-section properties, mean/equivalent cylinder-wall pressure, and equivalent total normal contact force, then explain how the simplified result relates to sealing and why it does not describe the complete local contact-pressure distribution.
